This bare HTML tag is escaped as text; use a raw HTML block if markup is intended.
Bidi override/isolate control U+202E is preserved by canonical Carve but not written to the text and code of presentation output; remove it unless intentional.
This line begins like a tilde fence but parsed as plain text - the block did not open. Check this line's syntax and any unterminated fence above it.

This quote is indented 1 column past the content column of document, and it still opens a quote, measured from its own line. Remove the indentation to make the structure explicit, or escape the opener to keep the line as text.
This line looks like a heading but directly follows text, so it is part of the paragraph or caption above it. Add a blank line before it.
A blockquote marker must be bare `>` or followed by a space. This line is literal text; write `> +` to quote it.
This braced span did not open: the delimiter inside it closed a span that started before it. Escape that delimiter.
Cross-reference </#{^> has no matching heading id; it renders as the literal text "</#{^>".
Link to "#nope" matches no id in this document, so the link goes nowhere.
Bare 4-colon fence has a different width from the innermost 3-colon div opened at 1:3; it closes the container.
This line starts with a percent run and holds other text, so it is content of the comment block and does not close it. Put the closing run alone on its line.
A line comment starts inside this reference label and takes the rest of the line, so the brackets are text. Move the comment out of the label, or escape the percent signs.
A line comment is text inside a line block. Use the braced comment.
This span looks like a C comment; use Carve comment syntax if you meant a comment.
A definition is recognized only at column 0 outside every container, so this line is text. Put it at column 0 outside every container.
A quote mark or list marker after the term mark is term text. Put the intended block on a `: ` description line at the list column, such as `: > text` or `: - item`.
A bare equals pair is text in 0.2. Write the braced highlight.
A bare tilde pair is text in 0.2. Write the braced strike.
A bare underscore pair is text in 0.2. Write the braced underline, or the slash pair for emphasis.

The table cell alignment prefix "<" is the deprecated 0.1.13 spelling, removed in 0.2.0. Alignment symbols now lead the cell's attribute block: write "{<}". In 0.2 the old prefix is cell text, so the formatter leaves it; the upgrade tool rewrites it.
The plus continuation marker was removed in 0.2 and is text here. If a block was intended, write that block after a blank line.

This indented line directly below a heading is part of the heading in 0.2; in 0.1 it started a paragraph. Remove the indent to make it a separate block again; if it then reads as a list marker or another opener and a paragraph is meant, escape its first character.
The loose attribute was removed in 0.2 and is a plain attribute here. A list is loose when a blank line stands between two of its items.
The separator row was removed in 0.2 and is a row of dashes here. Mark the header cells with the header mark and delete this row.
A spaced thematic break was removed in 0.2; this line is a list item (or text). Write the unspaced star form.
The substitution arrow was removed in 0.2; this is a strike span. Write a deletion directly followed by an insertion.
This description starts at column 1, below the column 4 of the definition list above, so it adds no entry to that list. Indent it to column 4 to continue the list.
This line continues the term above. Add a blank line after the term if it is a paragraph.
This emphasized paragraph looks like a heading.
This * closes no span, so it and the attribute block after it stay text. Brace the span you mean ({*text*}{…}) to attach the block, or escape the * to keep both as text.
This link has an empty destination.
This line is a footnote label and colon with no body, so it is text and defines no footnote. Add body content after the colon, or remove the line.
This line closes the block opened on line (n) although it is indented differently. If it is content, make the outer fence longer.

message: A "::: figure" inside a composite figure does not nest; it renders as a generic container. Move it out of the enclosing group.

A "::: figure" opener carrying a quoted title or [label] is not a figure group; it is a plain container with the class "figure" (C2-B-127). Drop the title or label to open a figure group, and use a caption line below it.
This "::: figure" group holds a single panel; a plain captioned figure renders the same content without the group wrapper.

This "::: footnotes" marker is inside a container, where it does not place: it renders as a plain typed div and the endnotes section goes where it would without the marker. Move the marker to document level, or delete it to accept the default position.
Three hyphens on line 1 open frontmatter, not a thematic break. Write three stars for a break.

trigger:
# Troubleshooting a 502 Response

A 502 response from nginx usually means it could not get a valid response from the upstream application.

> [!WARNING]
> Reload nginx only after validating the configuration. An invalid configuration can interrupt traffic.

```nginx
location / {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
}
```

## Checks

- Confirm the application is running and listening on `127.0.0.1:3000`.
- Check the nginx error log for connection failures or upstream timeouts.

After making a change, repeat the [Checks](#checks).

message: This spelling does not create a GitHub alert in Carve; use an admonition fence for an alert.
This strong span looks like a file glob; escape the asterisk if you meant a glob.
The closing "#" run is heading text in Carve, not a closing marker. Delete it.
This heading skips from level 1 to 3; use the next heading level for a continuous outline.
Trailing "{.c}" on a heading is literal text in Carve, not an attribute block. Move it to a "{.c}" line directly above the heading.
Four-space indentation does not make a code block in Carve; this renders as a paragraph. Use a ``` fence.

message: The gap after this label prevents the parenthesized destination from attaching; write `](` with no space for an inline link. A defined shortcut reference can still resolve the label.

This block opener is past the list item's canonical content column 3; it now parses structurally and the formatter will canonicalize it. Dedent it to column 3 for an explicit structural spelling, or escape the opener to preserve the literal meaning used by older readers.
This line is indented past the list marker but short of the item's text, and it belongs to the item. Indent it to the text, or move it to the column of the list to end the item.

This list marker starts at column 3, between the columns of two open lists, so it is read at the column of the deeper list. Start it at column 4 to make that explicit, or at column 1 to put it in the outer list.
This list marker is part of the preceding paragraph; add a blank line before the list.
This markdown definition remains paragraph text; use a :: term line before the definition.
Markdown `~~strikethrough~~` is literal text in Carve. Carve strikethrough is the braced `{~x~}`.
Markdown `**strong**` is literal text in Carve, asterisks included. Carve strong is a single `*`.
Use descriptive link text or a specific aria-label.
This one-letter marker fixes its list style, so the next marker starts another list.
This marker sits left of its list, so it is a sibling item that moves the list's column. Write the ordered markers left-aligned, as the formatter does.
This "::: references" marker is inside a container and does not place the reference list. Move it to document level, or remove it if no placement is needed.
Carve has no underline heading: this marker run is text. Write the heading with a leading `=`.
A mention or tag does not start directly after a letter or number. Put a space or punctuation before it.
A row attribute is the brace block glued after the closing pipe. Here it is cell content.
This table row has 2 cells; the first row has 1. Add or remove a cell to match the table.
This table-shaped line lacks a closing pipe and stays as paragraph text. If a table row was intended, write a complete row where a table can start.
The "^" span marker cannot extend a cell. It stands in the first row of its group: head, body or foot. It is a cell that holds "^" as text; escape it as "\^" to say so, or remove it.
This "^" joins the cell above it, so its attribute block applies to no cell and carve fmt drops it. Move the attributes to the cell it joins, or remove them.
This line of "___" is text in Carve 0.2. Write "***" for a thematic break.
This attribute line reaches no block: a blank line or the end of its container follows, so the line is text (C2-B-192). Move it directly above the block it describes, or delete it.

This caption line is not directly below an image, table, code block, quote, math block, figure group or code include, so it is text. If a blank line separates it from such a block, remove the blank line; otherwise escape the caret.
This attribute block is attached to nothing and renders as text. Glue it to a span, link or code span, or escape the brace.
This braced comment is not closed before the next block starts, so it stays text. Close it inside its block, or use %% line comments.
This strong opener is unclosed in its paragraph; add a closer.
Footnote reference [^[g] has no matching definition; it renders as literal text.
Reference link [g][h] has no matching link definition or heading; its brackets and label remain literal, while link-text children render normally.
Footnote definition [^n] is never referenced, so it is omitted from the rendered document.
This link reference definition is unused.
